clue.text: Colourful accessory indeed for peacock

parts.note: a sash is a bright band of cloth worn across the body or round the waist
ay (or aye) is an old word of assent, yes indeed

explanation.surface: A bright accessory really suits a showy bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peacock' is not the bird but a verb: to peacock is to strut and show off.
explanation.definitionFit: To peacock is to parade oneself showily, and to sashay is to swagger along in a flamboyant way.

clue.text: Send message at arm's length

parts.note: read literally, a signal sent by holding flags out at the full stretch of the arms

explanation.surface: Someone communicates while keeping their distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At arm's length' sounds like aloofness, but the flag signaller literally holds the message out with outstretched arms.
explanation.definitionFit: This flag-signalling system spells words by the positions of the arms holding two flags.

clue.text: Farewell order from the field

explanation.surface: A goodbye given as a player is ordered off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell party or gathering is this, and in football a referee dismissing a player from the pitch gives this order.

clue.text: Coal disease not unknown by name

indicators.note: not says the letter for the unknown is to be left out of the disease word

parts.note: anthrax is a serious bacterial disease of cattle and sheep
X is the mathematician's unknown quantity
to cite is to name or mention as an example

explanation.surface: A miner's lung complaint that isn't identified by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' signals the removal of the algebraic unknown from the disease; 'by' is only a link before the naming word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hard, glossy kind of coal that burns with little smoke.

clue.text: Console player who has to work Sundays

definitions.text: Console player who has to work Sundays

parts.words: Console player who has to work Sundays
parts.note: a console is also the keyboard desk of a church instrument, played at every Sunday service

explanation.surface: A video-gamer whose job keeps them busy at weekends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' suggests computer games; here it is the keyboards and stops of a church instrument, and church music means Sunday duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A church musician plays the pipe instrument from its console, and services fall on Sundays.

clue.text: Kind of course that needs a cold drink

explanation.surface: A training course is only bearable with a chilled drink to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A short course updating skills goes by this name, and the word is also slang for a reviving drink.

clue.text: Ben Travers excerpt sounds a cert

indicators.note: an excerpt is a piece taken out of a text, so the letters are lifted from inside the playwright's surname

explanation.surface: A Ben Travers farce passage sounds like a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers wrote British stage farces. 'Sounds a cert' is a pun: said aloud, 'a cert' is 'assert', which this word means.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert, which 'a cert' sounds like, is to declare something firmly as true.

clue.text: Mix one negus — nothing fiery

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: mixing a drink is a fair way to say its letters are to be stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: negus is a hot drink of port or sherry
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A barman makes a negus that turns out not to be warming at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' rearranges I (one), NEGUS and O (nothing). Negus is an old hot drink of wine, sugar and spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks of this kind formed from molten lava or magma, so the word means produced by fire.

clue.text: Tendency to come up with right conclusion

annotationWithheld.why: Tendency to come up with right conclusion (5): R (right) + END (conclusion) is clear, but no clue word gives the leading T of TREND, and no reading of 'to come up' yields it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Tendency to come up with right conclusion

clue.text: One of the teachers impervious to Dan

definitions.text: One of the teachers impervious to Dan

parts.words: One of the teachers impervious to Dan
parts.note: recalls the Victorian rhyme about two headmistresses whom Dan Cupid's darts could not touch

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher who resists the advances of a man named Dan.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Cupid is the god of love. The rhyme 'Miss Buss and Miss Beale, Cupid's darts do not feel' mocked two pioneering Victorian headmistresses of girls' schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances Mary Buss founded the North London Collegiate School and is half of a famous rhyme about unromantic schoolmistresses.

clue.text: Canadian university has no internal degree, but great spirit

indicators.note: has no internal says a piece buried within the longer string is taken out

parts.note: Manitoba is a Canadian prairie province, as in the University of Manitoba
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A Canadian college lacks an in-house qualification but has a fine spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no internal' signals removing the degree from inside the province-plus-university string, not from its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Among Algonquian peoples this is the name for a supernatural power or the Great Spirit.

clue.text: General's son can somehow escape outside? He did!

indicators.note: outside says the escape word goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: to flee is to escape by running away

indicators.note: somehow says the word can is to be put in some other order

explanation.surface: A soldier's boy manages to get away; and indeed he did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the can, and 'outside' wraps the escape word around it. In Macbeth, Banquo's son escapes the murderers, hence 'He did!'
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Macbeth, the boy who survives the ambush is the child of Banquo, one of Duncan's generals.

clue.text: Robber who gave his victims a fit at bedtime

definitions.text: Robber who gave his victims a fit at bedtime

parts.words: Robber who gave his victims a fit at bedtime
parts.note: the Greek bandit stretched or lopped his guests to fit his bed exactly

explanation.surface: A burglar so frightening that his victims had a seizure at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave his victims a fit' sounds like a scare; the legendary Greek brigand literally made each guest fit his bed, stretching or cutting them.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this bandit forced travellers to match his bed's length, until Theseus killed him.

clue.text: Mahogany, would you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: taken as written, the word to be pronounced

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone would pronounce the name of a timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a reddish-brown hardwood timber, a type of the material trees provide.

clue.text: One of Handy's large, clean characters

indicators.note: characters here are letters, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reference to one of Thomas Hardy's big, upright figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like part of the definition but signals rearranging LARGE and CLEAN. Angel Clare is the man Tess marries in Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: In Tess of the d'Urbervilles by Thomas Hardy, this parson's son marries and then deserts the heroine.

clue.text: Policeman not attached to the cooler

parts.note: something off is detached or disconnected
an icer is something that chills

explanation.surface: A constable who keeps his distance from the prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cooler' is slang for prison, which fits a policeman, but here it simply means something that ices.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is addressed as this, the general term for a member of the force.

clue.text: Such men were in league in one adventure

definitions.text: Such men were in league in one adventure

parts.words: Such men were in league in one adventure
parts.note: refers to a Sherlock Holmes story about a sham society open only to men with ginger hair

explanation.surface: A group of conspirators who banded together for an escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In league' sounds like conspiracy; it is the League of Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes story, a fake club for ginger-haired men.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holmes adventure concerns a bogus league that recruits only men with flaming ginger hair.

clue.text: Opera boy holds key to the earnest-money

indicators.note: holds says the boy's name contains the key

parts.note: Hansel is the boy in Humperdinck's opera Hansel and Gretel
D is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A boy at the opera keeps a key to a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is only a link. Handsel is an old word for a first payment or pledge made to seal a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest-money is a pledge paid to bind a deal, and this archaic word names such a first payment or gift.

clue.text: The ground factor in England at war

indicators.note: at war suggests turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A key element in England when the country was fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'war' rearranges ENGLAND and AT. A factor, in Scotland especially, is a steward who manages an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is an estate steward, and this person manages farmland and property for its owner.

clue.text: On fire, but went out a lot inside

indicators.note: inside says the hundred goes within the word for left

parts.note: to exit is to go out, so exited is went out
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for a lot

explanation.surface: Something was ablaze, yet a flame kept going out repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On fire' and 'went out' look like a fire dying; 'On fire' means thrilled, and C (100, a lot) goes inside EXITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on fire, figuratively, is being fired up and full of eager enthusiasm.

clue.text: Blackguard on state body

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a blackguard
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A scoundrel sitting on a government body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State body' looks like an official institution; 'state' is a verb and 'body' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse, especially one used for dissection, is a dead body.

clue.text: Ladies' seminary has the right dictionary for each name

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A girls' college keeps the correct dictionary for each name.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a famous English girls' boarding school on the Sussex coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminary is an old word for a school for young ladies, and this is a celebrated girls' boarding school near Brighton.

clue.text: Be eager to see hunt assembling

indicators.note: assembling means putting together, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Keen to watch the hunt gathering at the meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' looks like the hunt gathering but rearranges SEE and HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or behave with great excitement and keenness is to show one is eager.

clue.text: Skirting business started by daughter

indicators.note: started by says the daughter's letter comes at the front

parts.note: ado is fuss or business

explanation.surface: A shop dealing in skirting boards was begun by a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirting' is skirting board, the panel along the bottom of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of an interior wall, often finished with a rail or skirting.

clue.text: A natural belief from the foreign doctrine

parts.note: de is French for of or from
an ism is a doctrine or system of belief

explanation.surface: A belief about nature borrowed from a foreign creed.
explanation.walkthrough: This belief rejects revelation and holds that reason and nature alone show God exists; hence 'natural belief'.
explanation.definitionFit: This faith in a creator rests on reason and observation of nature rather than revelation or scripture.

clue.text: Pottery made from clay by peasant, say

parts.note: terra is Latin for earth, the soil or clay

indicators.note: say signals that the peasant word is pronounced, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a cotter is a peasant who rents a cottage

explanation.surface: Clay pots made by a farmworker, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRA (earth or clay) comes first; 'say' gives COTTA, which sounds like COTTER, a cottage-dwelling peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is unglazed brownish-red earthenware used for pots and roof tiles.

clue.text: Collar a hooligan, say

indicators.note: say signals that the hooligan word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a rough is a hooligan or thug

explanation.surface: Grab a yob, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like a verb meaning arrest a thug; it is a noun, the frilled neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a pleated starched frill worn round the neck in Elizabethan times.

clue.text: Pastry left to cool outside

indicators.note: outside says the cooling word goes around the letter for left

parts.note: to fan is to cool with a current of air

explanation.surface: Set the pie aside to cool outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' sounds like putting the pastry outdoors; it means FAN (to cool) goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling.

clue.text: A feeble person with no force

explanation.surface: Someone weak with no strength left.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: IN-va-lid, a sick person, and in-VAL-id, not legally valid.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick or disabled person is one sense; the other, stressed differently, means void or not legally binding.

clue.text: Give special prominence to the chin, for example

explanation.surface: Bring a jaw into the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight something is to make it a centrepiece, and a part of the face like the chin or nose is one of these.

clue.text: Liquor distilled in northern Madeira

indicators.note: distilling transforms a liquid, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spirit produced in the north of the island of Madeira.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distilled' fits liquor but rearranges MADEIRA with N (northern). 'Liquor' here is the liquid food is soaked in.
explanation.definitionFit: In cooking, a liquor is a liquid, and this seasoned liquid of wine, oil and spices is soaked into meat.

clue.text: Exercise, tear about — and wish you hadn't!

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around, so the pieces are rearranged

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a rent is a rip or tear

explanation.surface: Doing a workout and rushing around, then regretting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges PE (exercise) and RENT (tear).
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sorrow and remorse for one's past deeds is to regret them deeply.
